title: Hyderabad auto drivers call a day-long bandh on Nov 30

slides.head: Hyderabad auto drivers call a day-long bandh on Nov 30
What happened
slides.body: Demands include revised meter charges, a ban on green cabs, a crackdown on the auto black market and ₹36,000 per driver (₹12,000 a year) as promised.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The JAC says new cab and bike-taxi services are hurting drivers' earnings and that the promised fare revision hasn't come.

slides.head: auto bandh date
slides.body: They also want bike taxis banned in the city, like in Bengaluru.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: Drivers want ₹36,000 each, at ₹12,000 a year, as promised by the government.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether talks with the Transport Minister before Nov 30 lead to the bandh being called off, as in August. Ask: How would revised meter fares change a typical short auto ride?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
Hyderabad auto drivers call a day-long bandh on Nov 30

The Mahatma Gandhi Telangana Auto Drivers JAC wants revised meter fares implemented within 15 days, or the Transport Minister's resignation, and has called a bandh on Nov 30.

Why it matters: The JAC says new cab and bike-taxi services are hurting drivers' earnings and that the promised fare revision hasn't come.

Source: Siasat. Image: Siasat
